title: Read the failing items themselves
statement: Read the failing items and the judge's own reasoning, not just the scores and flag fields, because a summary can hide what failed and why.
example: In one run, 65 of 76 lesson bundles scored 0 on repetition while every list of repeated item ids was empty.
detail: An evaluator run over 76 lesson bundles of a reading course scored non-repetitiveness at an average of 0.14, with 65 of 76 at exactly 0, yet its lists of repetitive item ids were empty everywhere; the flags were only in its prose reasoning. The same reasoning showed that 9 bundles scored 0.0 because they were multi-passage by design and were judged against one passage, which reflects how the content was packaged for evaluation rather than item quality.

evidence.quote: Non-repetitiveness is by far the weakest dimension: **avg 0.14; 65 of 76 bundles scored exactly 0** on it.
Note `repetitive_item_ids` arrays are empty everywhere despite the 0 scores — the flags live in the prose reasoning, not the ID list.
9 bundles got overall score 0.0 (or 0.1 for mastery-formC):
These bundles are BY DESIGN multi-passage (MAP forms, mastery checks, spaced review) — the 0.0 reflects how the content was packaged for evaluation, not necessarily item quality.
The menacing model judgment itself contains an error: it calls the rollercoaster “fun screams,” whereas the actual option only says riders scream.
